newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sony profit doubles, sees record gain for year.
newsitem.headline: Sony profit doubles, sees record gain for year.

text.p: Sony Corp said on Wednesday that its group net profit nearly doubled in the three months to December, buoyed by strong sales of a videogame player and a weaker yen against the dollar.
The electronics giant also predicted it will post a record profit for the business year ending on March 31.
Sony unveiled a group net profit of 75.38 billion yen ($612 million) for October-December, up from 37.24 billion yen ($302 million) in the same period a year earlier.

It sharply increased its group net profit forecast for the full year to March to a record 132 billion yen ($1.07 billion) on strong sales of souped-up videogame players, minidiscs and camcorders, and also on the weak yen.
Sony said in a statement that the yen's year-on-year decline against other currencies increased its October-December group sales by about 110 billion yen ($894 million).
In the previous year, Sony's group net profit totalled 54.25 billion yen ($441 million).
The latest revised forecast was in line with last week's remarks by company president Nobuyuki Idei, who said that group sales and operating profits would reach record highs this business year.

"We will definitely see record high group sales and operating profits in the current business year," Idei told Reuters in an interview. "Many digital products, such as minidiscs and camcorders, are selling very fast."
Sony's quarterly group operating income from its mainstay electronics business rose 42.3 percent, helped by strong sales of its cutting-edge 32-bit home game player the PlayStation.
In its entertainment units, Sony's group operating income grew 13.6 percent to 31.7 billion yen ($257 million).
Sony's entertainment revenues come largely from its troubled Hollywood film-making unit Sony Pictures Entertainment and record unit Sony Music Entertainment.
Sony overhauled its Sony Pictures management last year, naming new heads of Sony Pictures and both its subsidiaries, Columbia Pictures and TriStar Pictures.
The higher income from the entertainment business reflects the strong performance of the music unit outside Japan as well as the yen's depreciation, Sony said.
Continued strong worldwide sales of Celine Dion's "Falling Into You" led the quarter's sales growth. Albums from the Fugees, Julio Iglesias, Babyface, and Journey also contributed to sales.

In the pictures group, sales increased significantly, benefiting from strong video sales of "Matilda" and "Jumanji" as well as the successful off-network syndication sale of the hit comedy "Mad About You", it said.
"However, several U.S. theatrical film releases during the quarter had disappointing box office performances," it added.

In a breakdown by geographic area, Sony group sales and operating revenue in the United States topped the list at 489.7 billion yen ($3.98 billion), up 31.8 percent from the same period a year earlier, followed by Japan's 459.8 billion yen ($3.73 billion), up 21 percent.
Meanwhile, group sales and operating revenue in Europe rose 17.4 percent to 409.1 billion yen ($3.32 billion).
"Overseas sales rose significantly in all geographic areas due to overall sales advances of electronics products as well as favourable sales in the entertainment business," Sony said.
